text: In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, write down the name of this day, this very day. On this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem.
Now speak a parable to the rebellious house and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: Set on the pot, set it on, and pour water into it.
Gather the pieces into it, every good piece, thigh and shoulder; fill it with the choicest bones.
Take the choicest of the flock, and pile the wood beneath it. Bring it to a boil, and cook the bones inside it as well.

versions.text: Take the choicest of the flock, and pile the logs beneath it. Bring it to a boil, and cook the bones inside it as well.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew here reads "the bones" (הָעֲצָמִים), not "logs"; "logs" reflects a conjectural emendation to עֵצִים. "Wood" is a smoother rendering of that emendation, but a footnote should be added noting that the Hebrew text reads "bones" and that many understand it as wood for the fire, so readers are not misled about the underlying text.

text: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the city of blood, the pot whose corrosion is in it, whose corrosion will not come off! Empty it piece by piece; no lot has fallen on it.
For the blood she shed is still within her. She poured it on the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground, to cover it with dust.
To stir up wrath and take vengeance, I have set her blood on the bare rock, so that it would not be covered.
Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the city of blood! I too will make the fire blaze high.

versions.text: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the city of blood! I too will make the pile great.
versions.explanation: "Make the pile great" is unclear when read aloud, since "pile" here refers to the heap of burning fuel (מְדוּרָה, a pyre or fire-heap), not to the pieces of meat mentioned earlier. A rendering that names the fire keeps the image intelligible for hearers and prepares for verse 10's "heap on the wood, kindle the fire."

versions.text: I too will make the fire blaze high.
versions.explanation: The opening two-thirds of the verse has been dropped: לָכֵן כֹּה אָמַר אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה ("Therefore thus says the Lord GOD") and אוֹי עִיר הַדָּמִים ("Woe to the city of blood"). The divine speech formula and the woe-oracle address are essential content; only the final clause remains. The earlier revision's intentional change (naming the fire rather than "the pile") is preserved.

text: Heap on the wood, kindle the fire, cook the meat thoroughly, mix in the spices, and let the bones be burned.
Then set the pot empty on its coals, so that it grows hot and its copper glows, its filth melting away inside it, its corrosion consumed.
It has frustrated every effort; its heavy corrosion will not come off—into the fire with its corrosion!
Your uncleanness is depravity. Because I would have cleansed you and you were not cleansed of your filth, you shall not be clean again until I have satisfied my wrath on you.
I, the LORD, have spoken. It is coming, and I will act. I will not hold back, I will not spare, I will not relent. According to your ways and your deeds they will judge you, declares the Lord GOD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, I am about to take from you the delight of your eyes with a single blow. Yet you shall not mourn or weep, and no tears shall come.
Groan in silence; make no mourning for the dead. Keep your turban on your head and your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your lips, and do not eat the bread of mourners.

versions.text: Groan in silence; make no mourning for the dead. Keep your turban on your head and your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your mustache or eat the bread of mourners.
versions.explanation: "Cover your mustache" is a literal rendering of a mourning gesture (veiling the lower face) but sounds odd read aloud; "cover your lips" or "cover the lower part of your face" communicates the customary sign of grief more clearly. A brief footnote explaining the gesture as a customary mourning rite would help, and the same wording should then be used in verse 22 for consistency.

versions.text: Do not cover your lips, and do not eat the bread of mourners.
versions.explanation: Three clauses of the Hebrew have been lost: הֵאָנֵק דֹּם ("Groan in silence"), מֵתִים אֵבֶל לֹא־תַעֲשֶׂה ("make no mourning for the dead"), and פְאֵרְךָ חֲבוֹשׁ עָלֶיךָ וּנְעָלֶיךָ תָּשִׂים בְּרַגְלֶיךָ ("bind your turban on you and put your sandals on your feet"). Only the last two commands remain. The restored wording keeps the intentional change from "cover your mustache" to "cover your lips."

text: So I spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died. And in the morning I did as I was commanded.
Then the people said to me, "Will you not tell us what these things mean for us, that you are doing this?"
I said to them: The word of the LORD came to me:

Say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am about to profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes, the yearning of your soul. And the sons and daughters you left behind will fall by the sword.
Then you will do as I have done: you will not cover your mustache or eat the bread of mourners.
Your turbans will stay on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away in your guilt and groan to one another.
Ezekiel will be a sign for you; you will do everything he has done. When it comes, you will know that I am the Lord GOD.
And you, son of man—will it not be on the day I take from them their stronghold, their joy and their glory, the delight of their eyes and the longing of their souls, their sons and their daughters—

versions.text: And you, son of man: on the day I take from them their stronghold, their joy and glory, the delight of their eyes and the longing of their souls—their sons and their daughters—
versions.explanation: The interrogative particle הֲלוֹא ("is it not?") is dropped, losing the rhetorical force that binds verse 25 to verse 26. Restoring it also smooths the transition into "on that day" in the following verse.

text: on that day a fugitive will come to you to bring the news to your ears.
On that day your mouth will be opened to the fugitive; you will speak and be silent no longer. So you will be a sign for them, and they will know that I am the LORD.
